subject: physics
question_text: Give the expression for the excess pressure in an air bubble inside the liquid.

mark_split.label: The bubble has one liquid surface

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2020 (Q5) and March 2025 (Q5) — Section A, 2 marks each time. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: an air bubble inside a liquid has liquid on the outside only, so there is ONE liquid–air surface and ΔP = 2T/r — the same expression as a liquid drop, and NOT the 4T/r of a soap bubble in air, which is a film with two liquid surfaces. ΔP here is the excess over the local pressure in the liquid just outside the bubble, which itself already includes atmospheric pressure and ρgh.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Say the count: one liquid surface, because the liquid is outside only.
steps.why: The word bubble is what misleads. What sets the formula is the number of liquid–air surfaces, and here the air sits in a hole in the liquid, so there is only one.
common_mistakes: Writing 4T/r because the word bubble appears. Only a soap bubble in air has two liquid surfaces.
Saying the air inside is a second surface. A surface needs liquid on one side of it.

recall.must_convey: That an air bubble inside a liquid has liquid outside only, so it has one liquid surface, like a drop.
accept: same as a drop, not a soap bubble

steps.memory_tip: Air bubble in liquid: liquid on the outside only. One surface, not two.

steps.label: ΔP = 2T/r
lines: One surface gives one contribution of 2T/r:
ΔP is the pressure inside the bubble minus
the pressure in the liquid just outside it,
T is the surface tension of the liquid and
r is the radius of the bubble.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Same formula as the drop. Write it with T and r named.
steps.why: Because the surface count is one, the single-surface result 2T/r is the whole answer, and no factor of two is added.
common_mistakes: Confusing ΔP with the total pressure inside the bubble. The total also carries the atmospheric pressure and the ρgh of the liquid above the bubble.

recall.must_convey: That the excess pressure in an air bubble inside a liquid is 2T by r, with T the surface tension and r the radius.
accept: T is the surface tension, r the radius
reject: the liquid is on the outside only

steps.memory_tip: Drop and air bubble each have one surface, so they share the same 2T/r.

insider_note: Same formula as the liquid drop, so the mark turns on the reason: the examiner looks for one liquid surface stated, not just 2T/r.
